text: Dynamic inputs from various modalities, such as facial expression video sequences, are first captured.
Each video frame across the sequence is mapped directly to a distinct node.
Similarly, continuous audio speech signals serve as an alternative dynamic modality,
where short temporal audio segments are extracted as graph nodes.
Body gestures captured through motion capture data are also seamlessly supported,
transforming consecutive body pose frames into corresponding graph nodes.
The Learnable Graph Inception Network, or L-GrIN, processes these dynamic graph inputs.
The architecture learns the underlying graph connectivity directly from the data.
A fully connected graph structure is initially formed over the temporal sequence of nodes.
The learnable adjacency matrix optimizes its edge weights jointly during model training.
Graph inception modules apply multiscale graph convolutions alongside neighbor max-pooling to extract dynamic temporal features.
A learnable pooling mechanism combines the node embeddings into a compact, graph-level feature representation.
Finally, the classification layer evaluates the graph embedding to predict the recognized emotion state.
